headline: Dolly Parton's Book Program Expands in London After Her Death
meta_description: The Imagination Library doubles its reach in London, expanding from 5 to 10 boroughs and making books available to 157,000 more children monthly.
summary_short: Less than a month after Dolly Parton's death, her Imagination Library doubled its presence in London, bringing free monthly books to 157,000 more children.
body:
The Imagination Library, founded by Dolly Parton in 1995, has doubled its reach across London even as the legendary musician and philanthropist is no longer here to witness it. The program, which has distributed 330 million free books to children under five over three decades, announced it would expand from five of London's 32 boroughs to ten. This expansion makes an additional 157,000 children eligible to receive a free book each month, addressed to them by name and delivered directly to their homes. The Postcode Lottery, a U.K. charity, is funding the growth while the Dollywood Foundation provides the infrastructure—a model that has proven simple enough to work across borders and resilient enough to endure beyond its creator's lifetime.

The timing of the expansion reveals something deeper about what Parton built. Jeff Conyers, president of the Dollywood Foundation, said she "was constantly pushing us about how we get the Imagination Library to more and more children." This wasn't a program designed around Parton herself; it was built to outlast her. The approach is deliberately uncomplicated: no applications, no means tests, no reading assessments. Just books. Research shows that when children receive these monthly deliveries, parents report increased reading interest, and studies suggest stronger literacy skills develop compared to peers who didn't enroll.

The expansion arrives as early childhood literacy faces real challenges. In the U.S., 33 percent of eighth graders now score at "below basic" reading levels—the highest in 30 years of testing. British teachers report that nearly a third of preschool-age children can't properly interact with physical books, tapping and swiping pages as though they were screens. Against this backdrop, the Imagination Library's simple remedy—a real book in the mail, month after month—matters more than ever.
quick_facts: Imagination Library expanded from 5 to 10 London boroughs after Parton's death
330 million books distributed over 31 years since 1995 launch
157,000 additional London children now eligible for monthly free books
Program operates across 50 U.S. states, Canada, Australia, Ireland, and U.K.
